A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KAN-AD and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably despite the added multivariate evaluation and reorganized appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark, efficiency, ablation, sensitivity, and training-contamination results for KAN-AD, including Tables 2, 3, and 5 and Figures 5–10.

after.justification: v3 retains the original univariate experiments and adds original multivariate benchmark results in Section 4.7 and Table 6.

M1.justification: Section 4.7 adds a multivariate adaptation that reshapes channels into separate univariate instances and trains on their collection. This changes input handling and training application while retaining the Fourier mapping, CNN reduction, and projection pipeline.

E1.justification: v3 retains KPI, TODS, WSD, and UCR and adds multivariate evaluation on SMD, MSL, SMAP, SWaT, and PSM. Section 4.7 and Appendix B substantially extend coverage to multivariate server metrics, spacecraft telemetry, and water-treatment data.

E2.justification: The new Table 6 substantially broadens evaluated comparators by adding Informer, DLinear, Autoformer, FEDformer, and UniTS, alongside previously evaluated Anomaly Transformer and TimesNet. The original univariate comparator set remains intact.

E3.justification: The added multivariate evaluation uses Best F1 alone and measures parameter counts on MSL. The retained univariate evaluation still reports four accuracy metrics and UCR efficiency; its stated splits, training budgets, and inference batch size are unchanged.

E4.justification: The case study, hyperparameter sensitivity, preprocessing and function ablations, and training-contamination tests retain their evidence in Figures 5 and 7–10 and Table 5. The multivariate addition is a benchmark comparison, not a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent trials with different random seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting for Table 2. The new Table 6 introduces no additional run-count, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: Original numerical results and plotted findings are retained. Table 6 adds results across five multivariate benchmarks, including average Best F1 of 0.9076 for KAN-AD versus 0.8921 for UniTS, and 4,491 KAN-AD parameters on MSL. These are new-setting results, not improvements over v2 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: The Kolmogorov–Arnold foundation, Equations 1–12, and function definitions in Table 4 retain their mathematical content. Equations 6–9 move within the methodology discussion; no new or revised theorem, proof, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same smooth-function formulation, robustness, efficiency, and four-benchmark performance claims. The multivariate extension does not revise those central statements.

C2.justification: Section 4.7 adds the explanation that training across independent channel instances can learn generalized normal patterns and extend KAN-AD’s univariate strengths to multivariate data. Earlier mechanism explanations and interpretations of the original experiments remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The advertised code repository changes from issaccv/KAN-AD to CSTCloudOps/KAN-AD. Section 4.7 also identifies THUML’s Time-Series-Library as the multivariate implementation framework. Existing univariate implementation settings are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations and descriptions for the multivariate datasets and comparators, plus Nie et al. (2023) to motivate channel independence. These additions support the new evaluation; the established related-work discussion and central research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 4.7 and a multivariate appendix, regrouping the original appendices as A.1 and A.2. It also adds acknowledgments and a generic impact statement, updates affiliations and correspondence, and removes an unresolved citation marker. Most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the full-width multivariate Table 6, relocates Figures 6 and 7 within page 7, and moves Equations 6–9 earlier in Section 3.3. Existing figures retain their drawing content, and existing tables retain their structures.

improvement.justification: Section 4.7, Table 6, and Appendix B add useful evidence of multivariate applicability, with an explicit adaptation and matching dataset/comparator descriptions, while preserving the original experiments. The gain is limited because the new evaluation reports only Best F1, whose inflation problem both versions acknowledge in Section 4.1.4, and provides no uncertainty estimates.
